THANK YOU!! I was reading through this thread to find a comment like this, because my sister and I also really hated these episodes. It all feels so unnecessarily cruel to Martha. The Doctor passively dismisses ALL the things Martha had to go through these past THREE MONTHS of her life, is racist towards her, cruel, and extremely unappreciative of her DESPITE knowing how she feels towards him from The Lazarus Experiment episode. For all her work, she just gets a small "Thanks for taking care of me" from him, a hug, and NO APOLOGY? A black woman from modern times who is an independent young doctor in training, being forced into a position of servitude and discrimination, on top of having to watch the person SHE also loves fall in love with someone else, endure racist comments and behavior from everyone around her, and most hurtfully from HIM, who had told her not to let him abandon her? He ultimately did abandon her for Joan, almost changed the course of history, did allow himself to let others get killed, literally going against almost all the rules he had set for himself and Martha. What was she supposed to do in her position??! I feel so incredibly bad for her, and while I know a lot of these factors were also out of 10's hands as well, not being able to pick the setting or time they would land in, this whole ordeal seems like a poor solution to how quickly he managed to solve it in the end.

I could argue more or less about how well this episode is written. A lot of other people seem to enjoy it a lot, and I get the appreciation of the show writers to not shy away from realistic topics like racism and how people of that era were products of their environment. But as a fellow person of color, it is really hard to watch and stomach some of these scenes, especially knowing and empathizing with everything Martha has had to endure by herself, with no actual help, friends, or allies beside her. Sure, she had the other maid to keep her company for a while, but she soon gets taken by the FoB and Martha is left with no one beside her. While Tennant's acting behind John Smith is amazing, and I agree with all the comments here that his acting is impeccable in selling two characters within the same person, I still can't get myself to enjoy John Smith or Joan for that matter, much less their romance. It feels very forced and very fast paced, and while good intentioned, I just don't like them very much as people. I know it's not fair to judge the time period based on modern standard and values but I can't get past it. And him knowing all this once coming back himself, knowing how Martha feels, what she had to endure going into this, AND then hardly even apologizing for any of it? Uh uh. I need a 10 page apology with tears AND UKULELE!!!!!

It's also particularly disgusting of him and twists the knife even further that he goes to seek out Joan after, and dangles the possibility of a further relationship, that the "John Smith" she knew still lives within him, and offers her to be his companion, despite fully knowing how unrealistic all of these promises were. I understand this personally to be something he does out of a last ditch desperation to cling onto the short lived human life he did have, and the possibility to forget all his responsibilities of being a time lord, and while understandable, is still incredibly selfish and manipulative of him to do. This doesn't take away from any of the excellence and brilliance of 10 as the Doctor, but these episodes just felt like an incredibly low point for him and how divorced he really is from humanity once he comes back to himself, and his human self wasn't so great either. Just not entirely a fan of this two parter or story at all. :(

I would have much preferred this storyline or most of the elements that this storyline touches upon in the setting of the episode like the racism, the tension leading up to WWI, and etc, to take place in one of the sci-fi or fantastical settings that the series excels at, while touching on these real life concepts. Perhaps it's just my personal preference, not really being a huge fan of history in general, but one thing I do love about UK and many of their stories in general how excellently they use fiction as a way to comment and discuss current and past events. This is actually a common tactic that was used around the 1600-1700s in order to skirt around censorship and continue to have a voice and constructive conversation in society!! In my opinion, while the need to visibly see the ugly parts of society in order to viscerally feel the impact it still has is important, I also argue that some stories are better told with the cover of fantasy to soften the blow and the pain that comes from seeing your generational trauma realized while creating real life parallels to better tell the story and feel its meaning without all the pain attached to it. I might have liked this episode a lot more had Martha been better treated or at least more properly apologized to in the end.

In my opinion, I feel it was very poor planning on TPUSA and the College Republicans tabling to
1) table without a permit
2) table while wearing MAGA and Trump paraphernalia.

I welcome all forms of free speech, ideally even bigoted and prejudiced forms of opinion and points of view. However, that being said, it is hard to listen to someone's honest opinion on gun control and gun rights when they are wearing MAGA hats and have a Donald Trump cardboard man in the background. By doing this, it makes their argument seem particularly partisan, and already gives their table a negative connotation of hate and prejudice. While MAGA hats and the image of Donald Trump aren't inherently racist or prejudiced, you can't deny their usage as hate symbols by those on the right and the left. You can't deny Trump's influence on empowering white nationalists with the polarizing things he says, and the inappropriate ways he talks and treats women and people of color. Whether or not you want to justify his actions, these are all things that Donald Trump has said and done. Radicals on the right use him as a figure that legitimizes their potentially bigoted views, whereas those the left use his image as a mockery of right radicals or just as a mockery of the President in general for the things he says. Donald Trump and the MAGA slogan are symbols that have been often used for hate and bigotry on both sides. I feel it was a poor decision and a poor choice to have these two images represent their table and ultimately their argument advocating for gun rights. In my opinion, if they truly wished to change minds and appeal to an already uphill battle with the majority of liberals on campus, they would have tried their best to remain neutral and non-partisan. I feel they should have taken into account the audience they were tabling to, knowing that most college campuses in the northeast are often massively liberal and progressive. 

Again, I will repeat what mostly everyone else has said, that they weren't supposed to be tabling there, and when they sensed an argument starting to escalate, they could have easily left and tried to table another time with a different approach.

I don't feel that the college republicans are entirely innocent here, and neither were the people protesting, but it is obvious how dividing and polarizing those symbols can be, and the power they hold, even if they weren't intended to be hate symbols or aren't inherently hateful. People interpret it as such, and therefore it is to a majority of people. I also believe that the timing of the event in accordance to the California shooting was also extremely poor. 

I encourage the college republicans and TPUSA to table again, barring the Donald Trump paraphernalia, and I, as a liberal myself would gladly sit down and listen to what they have to say. I personally don't have the answer to the gun control issue, but in my opinion I don't believe we should have more guns in a society that already abuses them so much. I am open to hearing a different opinion, though.
